newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Market yawns over Telebras 10-mo net.
newsitem.headline: Market yawns over Telebras 10-mo net.

text.p: Brazilian telecoms giant Telebras SA's whopping 2.2 billion-real, 10-month consolidated net profit was as expected, but the market was pleasantly surprised by results at its Telecomunicacoes do Rio de Janeiro SA, or Telerj, unit, analysts said.
"Telerj was good, much better than expected," said Maxim Medvedovsky of Banco Icatu.
Telerj, the Telebras unit serving Rio de Janeiro state, showed a 69.9 million-real net profit in the January-October period, up from the 55.3 million-real net posted in the first nine months.
"It's a dramatic improvement over one month," said Jacopo Valentino of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Analysts who follow the company said Telerj's October earnings were boosted by a jump in net operating revenues in October as a result of personnel reductions.

Telerj said its payroll stood at 11,881 employees on October 31, down 1,443 workers from the end of 1995. In the same period, the entire Telebras system's workforce shrank by 2,500 to 90,073 employees.
While Telebras' earnings were mostly in line with market expectations, analysts pointed to the reduction in personnel as a promising sign in light of the federally owned firm's planned privatization.
"I don't know about the market, but it sure makes me happy," said one analyst, who asked not to be named. "It shows Telebras is moving in the right direction."

Analysts' year-end forecasts for Telebras range from a consolidated net profit of 2.67 billion reais to 2.92 billion reais, with revenues rising towards year's end due to rising traffic in the last two months and line growth during the year. "I think we will see higher traffic at year's end and growth in lines in service in the fourth quarter," said Sergio Misima of Banco Fator.

Some had expected the rise to begin last month. "Telebras' results were in line with market expectations but I found them a little disappointing," said Deutsche's Valentino. "I expected them to go up but I didn't see that."

Telebras preferred share, Brazil's benchmark stock, was trading down 0.77 percent at 77.30 reais while the firm's voting common or ordinary share was down 0.61 percent at 65.40 reais at 1614 local/1814 EST on the Sao Paulo bolsa.
Traders said the decline may be a combination of profit-taking and investors trying to force prices lower.
